scene.name: Spring cart · 20 N/m
assumptions: The canvas has no known global drawing scale; scale 70 pixels per meter is the schema default, and physical dimensions follow the notes and clarification answers rather than the sketch proportions.
The track is modeled as a fixed level box with its upper face at Y=0; the wall and track dimensions and depth are approximate.
The clarified cart body dimensions are 0.20 × 0.10 × 0.10 m. The two clarified 0.04 m diameter wheels are modeled as 0.02 m thick cylinders with axles along Z.
Cart mass is split equally among the body and two wheels, as clarified; wheels are freely hinged to the body.
The cart is constrained to translate along X by an ideal slider. Contact friction 0.6 is assumed so the wheels can roll; restitution is 0, with no rolling-resistance torque or air drag.
Spring damping is set to zero because none was specified. The spring uses the stated 0.30 m rest length and 20 N/m stiffness.
The cart starts 0.20 m to the right of the spring's rest position, at rest. The spring attachment points are level.
Recorded model output #35 with model-proposed slider alignment #39 applied before release from rest.

source.notes: Spring-return cart: a 0.5 kg cart with two wheels sits on a straight level track. A coil spring connects the cart to a fixed wall on the left; its rest length is about 30 cm and its stiffness about 20 N/m. The cart is pulled 20 cm to the right (arrow and marker) and released from rest, so the spring pulls it back and it oscillates along the track. Ignore rolling friction.
explanations: Recorded sketch and model assembly #35. Slider anchor correction #39 is applied in both runs; stiffness edit #36 changes 20 to 40 N/m. These are locally reproduced solver runs, not a new live interpretation.
Wheel contacts dissipate motion even with zero spring damping; compare the measured periods rather than assuming a lossless oscillator.
